text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- Pakistan was the seventh largest importer of cereals among 82 countries in the last two years, a U.S. Agriculture Department report said.
- Cotton exporters are expected to register deals of 20,000 375-lb bales with the state-run Export Promotion Bureau.
- Six people including four police were wounded in a clash between workers of two rival religious organisations in Lahore.
- The army have recovered illegal arms during a clean-up operation in Parachinar, where clashes between Sunni and Shi'ite Moslems went into a fourth day.
- A partial strike was observed in Karachi on Saturday at the call of the Mohajir National Movement and allied parties in protest at the defection of a deputy of the Sindh provincial assembly.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The recent devaluation of the rupee has pushed up prices by five percent.
- The feasibility study of the Iran-Pakistan gas pipeline is likely to take nine months.
FINANCIAL POST
- The government reduced import duty on timber to 10 percent from 65 percent.
- The Hub Power Company Ltd's second generator began commercial production.
THE NEWS
- The Afghan government said it had arrested 43 Pakistani "infiltrators" during fighting with Taleban forces in Kunar province.

- Afghan President Burhanuddin Rabbani's top commander Ahmed Shah Masood has held secret talks with former communist warlord General Abdul Rashid Dostum on forming an alliance against the Taleban forces.
- The sensitive price indicator for the week to September 9 showed an increase of 0.13 percent over the previous week.
THE NATION
- Ireland's national airline Aer Lingus will handle passenger operations for state-run Pakistan International Airlines at Heathrow airport from the middle of next month.
- Pakistan's exports increased 13.9 percent in August from July and were up 18.7 percent on August 1995 in dollar terms.
- Pakistan said it was ready to set up an export processing zone in the private sector in Uganda if offered an attractive incentive package by the Ugandan government.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
